dct_description_sm: Available also through the Library of Congress Web site as a raster image.
Includes annotations and detailed cross sections describing topographic features and areas accessible to tanks and foot traffic.
Japanese title and annotations in red and black pen-and-ink and blue pencil, mounted on cloth. English title and notes in red pencil.
Map for military strategy covering the eastern part of Peleliu Island. The shortwave direction measurement station is depicted in the center, with the surrounding islands, villages and coves.
Map was probably drawn by the Japanese Navy and later added translation and annotations by the U.S. Army.

Map for military strategy covering the eastern part of Peleliu Island. The shortwave direction measurement station is depicted in the center, with the surrounding islands, villages and coves. Includes annotations and detailed cross sections describing topographic features and areas accessible to tanks and foot traffic. Two pieces of paper typed in English are pasted on map. Map was probably drawn by the Japanese Navy and later added translation and annotations by the U.S. Army. The Battle of Peleliu, fought between the U.S. and Japan during the Mariana and Palau Islands campaign of World War lI, from September to November 1944, on the Island of Peleliu, part of the island country Republic of Palau.
